translations.text: Of the son of David, king of Israel.
To know wisdom and instruction, and to understand words of insight;
to receive turns of speech, to grasp true righteousness, and to set judgments right;
to give shrewdness to the innocent, and understanding and insight to young children.
When a wise man hears these things, he will become wiser, and a discerning man will gain guidance.
He will understand proverbs and profound sayings, the words of the wise and their riddles.

The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and all who practice it have good understanding. Proper worship of God is the beginning of discernment, but the ungodly despise wisdom and instruction.
Listen, my child, to your father's instruction, and do not reject your mother's teaching,
for your head will receive a crown of grace, and your neck a golden necklace.
My child, do not let ungodly men deceive you, and do not consent if they invite you
and say, “Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth without cause.
Let us swallow him alive like Hades, and remove his memory from the earth.
Let us seize his possessions of every kind and fill our houses with plunder.
Cast your lot with us; let us all have a common purse, and let our treasury be shared.”
My child, do not walk the road with them; turn your foot away from their paths.
For their feet run toward evil, and they are swift to shed blood.
For it is not in vain that they spread nets for birds.
For those who share in murder heap up evils for themselves; the destruction of lawless men is grievous.
These are the ways of all who act lawlessly, for through their ungodliness they destroy themselves.
Wisdom is praised at the exits of the streets, and speaks boldly in the public squares.
She is proclaimed on the tops of the walls, frequents the gates of the powerful, and speaks boldly at the city gates.
As long as the innocent follow righteousness, they will not be put to shame. But the foolish, who desire outrage, have become ungodly, hated wisdom, and become liable to rebuke.
“Look, I set before you the messages of my spirit; I will teach you my words.
For I called, and you did not listen; I spoke at length, and you paid no attention.
Instead, you treated my counsel with contempt and paid no attention to my rebukes.
From now on I will laugh at your destruction and mock you when distress and siege come upon you.”
And when turmoil suddenly comes upon you, and destruction comes like a storm, or when ruin comes upon you,
then you will call to me, and I will not listen to you. The wicked will seek me and will not find me,
because they hated wisdom and did not seek the fear of the Lord,
and were unwilling to heed my counsel and despised my rebukes.
From now on they will eat the fruit of their own ways and be filled with their own ungodliness.
Because they oppressed children, they will be slaughtered, and reproof will destroy the ungodly.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in confidence and rest without fear of any evil.
My son, if you receive the words of my commandment and store them within yourself,
your ear will listen to wisdom, and you will direct your heart toward understanding and pass it on to your son for instruction.
For if you call wisdom to yourself and raise your voice for understanding,
and if you seek it like fine silver and search for it like treasures,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his presence come knowledge and understanding.
He stores up salvation for the upright and watches over their steps,
to guard the paths of justice, and he will secure the paths of those who fear him.
Then you will understand righteousness and justice, and you will make straight every path of goodness.
For if wisdom enters your mind and you consider understanding good for your soul,
Good counsel will watch over you, and a holy mind will guard you.
for they will save you from the evil path and from the man who speaks nothing trustworthy.
Oh, those who have abandoned the straight paths to walk in paths of darkness,
who rejoice in evil things and delight in the perversity of wickedness,
whose ways are crooked and whose paths are perverse,
to lead you away from the straight path and estrange you from righteous counsel! My son, may evil counsels not reach you,
of those who have abandoned the instruction of their youth and forgotten the divine covenant.
For she placed her house near death and her paths near Hades, among those born of the earth.
All who go with her will not return, but will also come to repentance; yet they will not reach straight paths or attain the years of life.
For if he had walked in good paths, they would surely have found the easy paths of righteousness. Those who have become kind will inhabit the land; the innocent will remain in it.
For the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it.
The ways of the ungodly will perish from the earth, and the lawless will be driven out of it.
My child, do not forget my laws, and keep my words in your heart.
For length of life, years of living, and peace will be added to you.
Do not let mercy and faithfulness depart from you. Put them around your neck and write them across your heart.
And you will find favor; consider what is good before the Lord and before people.
Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not take pride in your own wisdom.
Acknowledge him in all your ways, so that he may make your paths straight, and your foot will not stumble.
Do not be wise in your own eyes, but fear the Lord and turn away from all evil.
Then there will be healing for your body and restoration for your bones.
Honor the Lord with your honest earnings, and bring him fruit from the crops you have gained justly.
So your storehouses will be filled with an abundance of wheat, and your winepresses will overflow with still more wine.
My child, do not lose heart under the Lord’s discipline, and do not give way when he rebukes you.
For the Lord disciplines those he loves; he chastises every child he accepts.
Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who has seen understanding.
For acquiring that merchandise is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more precious than precious stones, and there is nothing evil that can stand against her. She is known to all who draw near to her, and everything that is precious moves her.
For long days and years of life are at her right, and glory and greatness at her left. Righteousness flows from her mouth; she carries laws and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are ways of goodness, and all her paths are peaceful.
She is a tree of life to all who take refuge in her, and to those who lean steadfastly on her as on the Lord.
God laid the foundations of the earth with wisdom and prepared the heavens with counsel.
By his understanding he split open the depths, and the clouds poured out rain.
My child, do not grow weak; keep my counsels and wisdom.
So that your soul may live and grace may be upon your neck; there will be healing for your body and restoration for your bones.
For you will walk with the hope of peace in all your ways, and your foot will not stumble.
For if you sit down, you will be without fear, and if you sleep, your sleep will be sweet.
You will not fear terrors that come upon you or attacks by the ungodly that befall you.
For the Lord will watch over all your ways and make your foot firm so that it will not stumble.
Do not delay doing good to someone in need when you are able to help them.
Do not say, “Go away and come back, and tomorrow I will give,” when you are still able to do good, for you do not know what tomorrow will bring you.
Do not plot evil against your friend who relies on you and trusts in you.
Do not be hostile to anyone without cause, lest he do you harm.
Do not acquire the reproaches of evil men, and do not envy their ways.
For everyone who is lawless is detestable before the Lord and does not share fellowship with the righteous.
The Lord’s curse is on the houses of the ungodly; the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
The Lord opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted dishonor.
Children, hear a father’s instruction, and pay attention so that you may understand wisdom.
For I will give you good gifts; do not abandon my laws.
For I too was a son obedient to my father and beloved in the eyes of my mother.
Those who taught me said, “Let our word be firmly established in your heart; keep my commandments and live.”
Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding, and do not forget or disregard the sayings of my mouth, and do not turn aside from the words of my lips.
Do not abandon her, and she will shelter you; love her, and she will protect you.
The beginning of prudence: acquire wisdom, and in all your ways acquire understanding.
Surround yourself with her, and she will exalt you; honor her, so that she may embrace you.
For she will give your head a crown of grace, and with a crown of delight she will watch over you.
Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will multiply, and the paths of your life will increase.
I teach you the ways of wisdom; I give you understanding of straight paths.
For if you walk, your steps will not be hindered, and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Hold fast to my instruction and do not let it go; instead, keep it for your own life.
Do not walk in the ways of the ungodly, and do not envy the ways of the lawless.
Do not pass through the place where they dwell; turn away from them and avoid that place.
For they do not sleep unless they do evil; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not sleep.
They eat the food of ungodliness and become drunk on the wine of lawlessness.
The paths of the righteous shine like light; they lead the way and give light until the day becomes bright.
The paths of the ungodly are dark, and they do not know how they stumble.
My son, listen to my wisdom and incline your ear to my words.
So that your springs do not fail, keep them in your heart.
For they are life to those who find them and healing for all flesh.
Guard your heart with all vigilance, for from these life flows forth.
Put a crooked mouth far from you, and banish unjust lips from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids direct an honest gaze.
Make straight paths for your feet, and set your ways straight.

Do not turn aside to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from the evil path. For God knows the paths on the right, but the paths on the left are crooked. He himself will make your paths straight and lead you forward on your ways in peace.
My child, heed my wisdom and incline your ear to my words.
So that you may preserve good judgment, I instruct you in the wisdom of my lips. Do not look at an evil woman.
For honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, and for a time it pleases your palate.
But afterward she is found to be even more bitter than gall and sharper than a double-edged sword.
For the feet of the shameless woman bring those who associate with her down to Hades with death, and her footsteps are not firm.
For they do not follow the paths of life; her ways are wayward and unknown.
Now, my child, listen to me, and do not disregard my words.
Keep your ways far from her, and do not approach the doors of her house.
So that you do not surrender your life to strangers and your possessions to the merciless.
So that strangers do not have their fill of your strength, and the fruits of your labor do not enter the houses of others.
And afterward you will regret it, when the members of your body waste away.
And you will say, “How I hated instruction, and my heart turned away from rebukes!”
I did not listen to the voice of my instructor, and I did not incline my ear to my teacher.
A little more, and I would have been in the midst of every evil, in the midst of the congregation and the people.
Drink water from your own vessels and from the springs of your own wells.
Let your waters gush forth for you from your own spring, and let your waters flow into your public squares.
Let them belong to you alone, and let no stranger share them with you.
Let your spring of water be yours alone, and rejoice with the wife of your youth.
A loving doe and a colt that has your favor—let her converse with you and be considered your wisdom, and let her be with you at all times, for if you walk in her love, you will increase greatly.
Do not frequent strangers, and do not embrace a bosom that is not yours.
For a man’s ways are before the eyes of God, and he watches all his paths.
Lawless deeds trap a man, and everyone becomes entangled in the nets of his own sins.
He dies among the undisciplined because of his lack of discipline; he was deprived of the fullness of his life and perished because of his folly.
Son, if you become a guarantor for your friend, you have handed yourself over to an enemy.
For a man’s own lips are a powerful snare, and he is caught by the words of his own mouth.

Now, my son, do what I command you, and you will live. For you have fallen into the hands of evil people because of your friend. Now be strong and do not give up; urge on the friend for whom you have stood as guarantor.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids,
so that you may escape like a gazelle from snares and like a bird from traps.
Go to the ant, you lazy man, and imitate its ways, and become even wiser than it.
For it has no farming, no taskmaster, and is not under any masters,

yet it prepares its food in summer and lays up abundant stores at harvest. Or go to the bee and learn how industrious it is and how carefully it does its work. Kings and poor people use the fruit of its labor for healing. It is desired and honored by everyone, for although it is weak in strength, it has valued wisdom and has been honored.
How long will you remain [?], you lazy man, or when will you wake from sleep?
Sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, rest your hand a little on your chest.

Then poverty will come upon you like an evil traveler, and want like a swift messenger. But if you are diligent, your summer will come like a spring of water, and want will flee of its own accord like an evil man.
A lawless and foolish man walks crooked paths.
For he himself winks with his eye, signals with his foot, and gives instructions by signs with his fingers.
A perverse heart devises evil at all times; such a person causes disturbances in the city.
And because of this, his destruction will come upon him suddenly: injury and ruin without healing.
For he rejoices in everything the Lord hates, and he is crushed because of the uncleanness of his soul.
The eyes of an insolent person, an unjust tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
a heart that devises evil plans, and feet that hurry to do evil will be destroyed.
An unjust witness kindles falsehood and stirs up strife among brothers.
My son, keep your father’s laws, and do not reject your mother’s instruction.
Receive them into your soul and upon your head always, and place them like a necklace around your neck.
When you go, take it with you, and it will be with you. When you sleep, it will guard you, and when you rise, it will speak with you.
For the commandment of the law is a lamp and a light, and reproof and instruction are the way of life,
to keep you from a married woman and from the slander of a foreign tongue.
My son, do not let desire for beauty overcome you, and do not be caught by your own eyes or carried away by her eyelids.
For the price of a prostitute is the cost of a single loaf of bread, for an evil woman hunts the souls of honorable men.
Can anyone carry fire in his lap without burning his clothes?
Or can anyone walk on fiery coals without scorching his feet?
Likewise, whoever goes in to another man’s wife will not go unpunished, and no one who approaches her will be acquitted.
It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing: he steals to satisfy his hunger.
But if he is caught, he must repay sevenfold and give all his possessions to save himself.
But whoever commits adultery, through lack of sense, brings destruction upon himself.
He bears pain and dishonor, and may his disgrace never pass away.
Her husband’s fury is full of jealousy, and he will show no mercy on the day of judgment.
He will not exchange his hostility for any ransom, nor will he be appeased by many bribes.
My son, keep my words and store my commandments within yourself. My son, honor the Lord and be strong, and fear no one other than him.
My son, keep my commandments and you will live, and guard my words like the pupil of your eye.
Bind them around your fingers and write them across your heart.
Say that wisdom is your sister, and make understanding your close companion,
so that she may guard you from a strange woman and from an evil woman when she deceives you with words.
Leaning out of the windows of her house toward the streets,
whomever she sees among the foolish youths, a senseless one among the young men,
Who pass through the public squares, near the corner of the paths to her house.
she speaks with him in the evening darkness, when they are at rest in the darkness of night.
And the woman meets him dressed like a prostitute, bewildering the minds of young men.
Inflamed with desire and wanton, her feet do not remain at home.
For sometimes she wanders outside and sometimes in the streets; she lies in wait at every corner.
Then she seized him and kissed him, and with a shameless face she said to him,
I have vows of peace; today I fulfill my prayers.
“For this very reason I came out to meet you; longing to see your face, I found you.
I have fitted my couch with striped coverings and adorned it with Egyptian linens.
I have prepared my bed with sprinkled saffron and perfumed my house with cinnamon.
Come, let us enjoy love until morning; come, let us delight in desire,
for my husband is not at home but has gone on a distant journey.”
He has taken the bag of silver in his hand; only after many days will he return to his house, if at all.
She led him astray with many words and bewildered him with the snares of her lips.
He followed her foolishly, like an ox going to slaughter and like a dog caught in a net,
or like a deer struck by an arrow through the liver. He hurries like a bird into a snare, not knowing that he is going to his own destruction.
Now, my child, listen to me and heed the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways, and do not stray onto her paths.
For she has struck down many with wounds, and those she has killed are countless.
Her house is the road to hell, leading down to the chambers of death.
Therefore proclaim wisdom, so that understanding may speak to you.
For she is on the highest mountains and stands in the midst of the paths.
She waits at the gates of the mighty and gives blessings at the entrances.
I appeal to you, O people, and offer my voice to the children of humanity.
You who are simple, understand prudence; and you who lack instruction, take it to heart.
Listen to me, for I speak honorable things, and upright words flow from my lips.
For my throat will utter truth, and lying lips are abhorrent to me.
All the sayings of my mouth are righteous, and there is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
Everything is straightforward to the wise and fitting to those who find knowledge.
Accept instruction rather than silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
Wisdom is better than precious stones, and nothing precious is worth as much as she is.
I, wisdom, have dwelt in deep understanding; I have called counsel and knowledge to myself.
The fear of the Lord is to hate injustice, insults, pride, and evil ways.
Counsel and caution are mine; understanding and strength are mine.
Through me kings reign, and rulers write just decrees.
Through me the great become great, and rulers hold the earth through me.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find favor.
Greatness and glory are mine, as are abundant possessions and righteousness.
It is better to acquire me than gold and precious stones, and my fruits are better than choice silver.
I walk in the ways of righteousness and travel in the midst of the paths of justice.

For I will bestow greatness on those who love me and fill their treasuries with good things. If I tell you what is to happen day by day, I will also remind you of the things that have been reckoned from eternity.
The Lord acquired me at the beginning of his ways, for his works.
Before the ages he established me, from the beginning, before making the earth.
Before making the depths, before the springs of water gushed forth.
Before the mountains were established and before all the hills, he brought me forth.
The Lord made the inhabited and uninhabited places, and the inhabited reaches beneath heaven.
While he was preparing the heavens, I was with him, and while he was setting his throne upon the winds.
When he strengthened the clouds above, and when he firmly established the springs beneath heaven.
When he set his boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not pass beyond its shore, at the time when he firmly established the foundations of the earth.
I was beside him in harmony. I was the one in whom the Lord delighted continually, and I rejoiced before him at all times.
When he delighted in completing the universe, I rejoiced in the children of mankind.
Now, son, listen to me, and blessed are those who keep my ways.
Listen to wisdom and become wise, and do not be hemmed in.
Blessed is the man who listens to me, and the person who keeps my ways, who watches at my doors continually and guards the thresholds of my entrances.
For my paths are paths of life, and my desires are made ready by the Lord.
But those who sin against me act wickedly against their own souls, and those who hate me love death.
Wisdom built herself a house and erected seven pillars.
She slaughtered her animals, mixed her wine in mixing bowls, and prepared her table.
She sent her servants to invite people with a loud proclamation to her mixing bowls, and she says:
“Whoever is foolish, let him come to me.” And to those lacking understanding she says:
“Come, eat of my bread and drink my wine, which I have mixed for you.
Leave foolishness behind and live. Seek wisdom so that you may survive, direct your understanding through knowledge, and comprehend instruction by a straight path.”
Whoever instructs the wicked receives dishonor for himself, and whoever rebukes the ungodly hates himself.
Do not rebuke the wicked, lest they hate you. Rebuke the wise man, and he will love you; rebuke the foolish man, and he will hate you all the more.
Give a wise man reasons, and he will become even wiser. Instruct the righteous man, and he will take in more.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of the holy is understanding. Knowing the laws belongs to richly endowed minds.
In this way you will live a long time, and years of life will be added to you.

My child, if you become wise, you will be wise for yourself and for your companions; but if you are foolish, you alone will dig up troubles. Whoever relies on falsehood shepherds the winds and chases winged birds, for he has left the paths of his own vineyard and has strayed from the tracks of his own field. He travels through waterless country, through the wilderness, and through a land appointed for thirst, and gathers fruitlessness with his own hands.
A foolish and reckless woman will lack bread, and she knows no shame.
She sat at the door of her house on a chair, in plain view in the public squares.
She calls to passersby who go straight along their own paths.
“Whoever among you is most foolish, let him turn to me. To you who lack understanding I give a command and say:
Eat bread in secret with pleasure, and drink stolen water with delight.”

And he does not know that those born on earth perish with her and reach the depths of Hades. But you, leap away and do not linger in her place, and do not fix your eye on her, so that you may pass through foreign water and cross a foreign river and keep away from foreign water. Do not drink from a foreign spring, so that you may live a long time and years of life may be added to you.
PROVERBS OF SOLOMON
Second Discourse
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is a sorrow to his mother.
The treasures of the lawless will be of no help, but righteousness delivers from death.
The Lord does not let the righteous person starve to death, but he will destroy the lives of the ungodly.
Poverty brings a man low, but the hands of the diligent make him great.
A son who has been instructed will be wise and will make the foolish serve him. A wise son escapes the scorching heat; a lawless son is struck by the scorching heat in summer.
The Lord’s blessing is upon the heads of the righteous, but untimely sorrow will cover the mouths of the ungodly.
The righteous are remembered with praise, but the name of the ungodly will be extinguished.
A wise heart will receive commandments, but one who is reckless with his lips will stumble and be ruined.
Whoever walks with integrity walks confidently, but whoever makes his paths crooked will be exposed.
Whoever winks deceitfully brings sorrow upon men, but whoever rebukes openly makes peace.
A fountain of life is in the hand of the righteous, but destruction will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all who are not contentious.
Whoever pours forth wisdom from his lips strikes the foolish man as with a rod.
The wise keep wisdom hidden, but the mouth of the reckless is near ruin.
The possessions of the rich are a fortified city; poverty is the ruin of the ungodly.
The deeds of the righteous bring life, but the fruits of the ungodly bring sins.
The Lord guards the paths of life; instruction without correction leads astray.
Righteous lips conceal hostility, but those who spread slander are foolish.
By speaking much you will not escape sins; if you restrain your lips, you will be wise.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the ungodly will fail.
The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but the senseless will perish in want.
The Lord’s blessing is upon the heads of the righteous, and it makes a person great and adds no sorrow to his heart.
The foolish person does evil with laughter, but wisdom produces understanding in a man.
The ungodly walks toward destruction, but the desire of the righteous is accepted.
When the storm passes, the ungodly is destroyed, but the righteous escapes and will live forever.
As an unripe grape is harmful to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practice it.
The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the ungodly will be shortened.
The joy of the righteous endures, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
The fear of the Lord is strength for the holy and destruction for those who do evil.
The righteous will never tremble, but the ungodly shall not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous pours forth wisdom, but the tongue of the unjust will be destroyed.
The lips of righteous men will pour forth gracious words, but the mouth of the ungodly will be destroyed.
Deceitful scales are an abomination before the Lord, but an honest balance is acceptable to him.
Where insults enter, dishonor is also there, but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
The integrity of the upright will guide them, but the stumbling of the contemptuous will destroy them.
Riches will be of no help on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death. The righteous man died and left regret; the destruction of the ungodly comes very recklessly and with trampling.
The righteousness of the blameless makes their paths straight, but the unjust fall into ungodliness.
The righteousness of upright men delivers them, but the lawless perish through foolishness.
When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boasts of the ungodly will perish.
The righteous escapes from hunters, and the ungodly is handed over in his place.
In the mouths of the lawless is a snare for their neighbors, but the wisdom of the righteous succeeds.
Through the prosperity of the righteous a city was established, and at the destruction of the ungodly there was joy.
Through the blessing of the upright a city will be exalted, but through the mouths of the ungodly it will be destroyed.
A man lacking understanding despises his neighbor, but a wise man loves silence.
A double-tongued man reveals secrets in court, but one who is faithful in spirit conceals matters.
Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but deliverance is found in much counsel.
A senseless person does evil when he associates with a righteous person, and hates the voice of caution.
A gracious woman increases her husband's glory, but a woman who hates justice is a throne of dishonor. The cowardly fall from wealth into poverty, but the diligent are established in wealth.
A merciful man does good to his own soul, but a merciless man destroys his own body.
The ungodly performs works of injustice, but the offspring of the righteous is a reward of truth.
A righteous son is born to life, but the pursuits of the ungodly lead to death.
Crooked ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all who are blameless in their ways are acceptable to him.
Whoever attacks unjustly will not go unpunished, but whoever sows righteousness will receive a sure reward.
Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is the beauty of a woman of bad character.
The desire of the righteous is entirely for good, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
Some sow what they have and gain many times as much, while others gather unjustly and fall into poverty.
Every blessed soul is sincere, but an angry man is ugly in appearance.
Whoever hoards grain will leave it to strangers, and whoever withholds grain will be publicly cursed, but a blessing rests on the heads of those who distribute it.
Whoever plans good seeks the favor of goodness, but whoever seeks evil will have it come upon him.
Whoever trusts in wealth will fall, but whoever watches over the righteous will flourish.
Whoever does not [?] his own household will inherit winds, and the foolish will serve the wise.
From the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life, but the lives of the lawless will be taken away prematurely.
If the righteous are scarcely saved, where will the sinner and the wicked be found?
Whoever loves instruction loves wisdom, and whoever hates correction is foolish.
Good is the one who finds favor with the Lord, but a lawless man will be condemned.
A person will not prosper through lawlessness, but the roots of the righteous will not be cut off.
A diligent wife is a crown to her husband. Just as a worm damages wood, so an evildoing wife destroys her husband.
The counsels of the righteous are just; the wicked are guides in deceit.
The mouths of the wicked are deceitful, but the mouth of the upright will rescue them.
Whichever way the wicked turns, he is destroyed, but the houses of the righteous will endure.
The mouth of the wise is praised by people, but one with a twisted heart will be despised.
It is better for a person to serve himself humbly than to give himself airs and beg for bread.
A righteous person has compassion on his animal, but the hearts of the wicked are merciless.
Whoever works his land will have his fill of bread, but those who pursue worthless things lack understanding. Whoever delights in lingering over wine will leave disgrace in his dwelling.
The desires of the wicked are evil, but the roots of the godly are firm.

Through the wrongdoing of his lips, the sinner falls into a snare, but the righteous escapes it. One with a kindly look finds compassion, but whoever encounters others at the gates brings distress to souls.
From the fruit of a man's mouth, his soul will be filled with good things; the reward for his lips will be paid back to him.
The ways of fools seem right to them, but the wise person listens to instruction.
A fool reveals his anger at once, but a shrewd man conceals his disgrace.
The righteous person openly declares the truth; a witness for the lawless is deceitful.
Some wound with their words as with a sword, but the tongues of the wise heal.
Truthful lips establish testimony; a hasty witness has a dishonest tongue.
Deceit is in the heart of one who plots evil, but those who desire peace will be glad.
Nothing unjust pleases the righteous person, but the ungodly will be filled with evil.
Lying lips are an abomination before the Lord, but whoever acts faithfully is acceptable to him.
A wise man is a throne of understanding; the heart of fools will encounter curses.
The hand of the chosen will easily prevail; the deceitful will be handed over to be plundered.
A fearful word troubles the heart of a righteous man, but good news makes him glad.
The righteous person is discerning and loves himself; the counsels of the ungodly are [?]. Evils pursue sinners, good things come to the righteous, and the ways of the ungodly lead them astray.
No prey will fall to the deceitful person; a pure and generous man is a precious possession.
In the paths of righteousness there is life; the paths of those who bear grudges lead to death.
A shrewd son obeys his father; a disobedient son will come to ruin.
From the fruit of righteousness he will eat abundantly; the souls of the lawless will perish before their time.
Whoever restrains his mouth preserves his life, but whoever is reckless with his lips troubles his own soul.
Every lazy person is in need; the hands of the diligent have provisions.
The righteous person hates dishonest speech, but the ungodly person is ashamed and will find no confidence.
Righteousness guards those whose way is blameless; sins make the ungodly foolish.
Some exalt themselves but have nothing, and some humble themselves but are full of great wealth.
A man's wealth is the ransom for his life, but the poor person cannot endure punishment.
The light of the righteous shines at all times; the light of the ungodly will be extinguished. Deceitful souls will stray into sins, but the righteous will show compassion and mercy.
A fool does evil with insults, but those who are discerning about themselves are wise.
Wealth accumulated through injustice will diminish, but whoever gathers it through devotion to God will increase it.

It is better to help wholeheartedly from the outset than to promise hastily and leave someone waiting in hope. The righteous person shows mercy and lends. The desire for good things is a tree of life.

Whoever despises things will be despised by them; whoever fears the commandment will be sound. Let nothing good come to a deceitful son. A wise servant’s deeds will prosper, and his paths will be made straight.
The instruction of a wise person is a fountain of life, but the fool will die in a snare.
Good wisdom gives grace, and knowing the law belongs to good understanding. The path of those who show contempt leads to destruction.
Every prudent person acts with wisdom, but the fool brings evils upon himself.
A reckless king will fall into trouble, but a faithful messenger rescues him.
Instruction removes poverty and dishonor, and whoever heeds rebukes will be honored.
The desires of the godly delight their souls; the deeds of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
Whoever walks with the wise will become wise, and whoever gropes along with fools will become known.
Evils pursue sinners, but good things will come to the righteous.
A generous man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, and the wealth of the ungodly is stored up for the righteous.
The righteous will enjoy wealth for many years, but the unjust will perish quickly.
Whoever spares the rod hates his son, but whoever loves him disciplines him with care.
The righteous person satisfies himself with his food, but the ungodly remain in want.
Wise women built houses, but foolish women tore them down with their own hands.
Whoever walks uprightly fears the Lord, and whoever is crooked in his ways will be dishonored.
From the mouths of fools comes a rod of insults, but the lips of the wise will protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the mangers are clean; where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is evident.
A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness stirs up falsehood.
You may seek wisdom among the wicked and not find it, but you will easily find understanding among the wise.
Everything is contrary to a fool; wise lips are a weapon of understanding.
The wisdom of the prudent discerns their paths; the folly of fools is marked by error.
The houses of the lawless will require purification; the houses of the righteous are acceptable to him.
The heart of an understanding man is a sorrow to his soul, and when he rejoices, he does not join in insults.
The houses of the ungodly will be destroyed; the homes of the righteous will be blessed.
There is a way that seems right in people's eyes, but their end leads to the depths of hell.
Sadness does not mingle with joys, but afterward joy turns to mourning.
The hard-hearted person will have his fill of his own ways, and a benevolent man will be guided aright by his own counsels.
The innocent person believes every word, but the shrewd person comes to repentance.
The wise person takes fright and turns away from evil, but the fool confidently mingles with the lawless.
A hot-tempered person acts without thought, but a wise man is very patient.
The ungodly share in evil, but the shrewd grow strong through wisdom.
The wicked will stumble before the good, and the ungodly will plead at the doors of the righteous.
Friends will hate their poor friends, but the rich have many friends.
Whoever despises the needy sins, and whoever has mercy on the poor is blessed.
Those who go astray devise evil; good people devise mercy and truth. Those who devise evil do not know mercy and faithfulness; mercy and faithfulness are with those who devise good.
Everyone who takes thought about something has more wisdom, but the self-indulgent and carefree person will be in need.
The crown of the wise is shrewdness, and the conduct of fools is wickedness.
A faithful witness saves a life, but a deceitful person fans the flames with lies.
In the fear of the Lord there is hope of strength, and he leaves his children the security of peace.
The Lord's command is a fountain of life and makes one turn away from the snares of death.
A king's glory is in his many troops; the decline of the people is the downfall of the powerful.
A patient man has abundant understanding, but an impatient man is very foolish.
A gentle man is a healer of the heart; an anxious heart is like a moth in the bones.
Whoever oppresses the needy angers their Maker, and whoever honors him has mercy on the poor.
The ungodly person is cast out because of his own evil deeds, and whoever trusts in the purity of his own soul is righteous.
Wisdom rests in a good heart, but it is not known in the hearts of fools.
Righteousness raises up a nation; sins diminish nations.
A wise servant is acceptable to the king, and by his own promptness he shakes off dishonor; anger destroys the wise.
A gentle answer turns away wrath; a harsh word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise knows good things, but the mouths of fools recount evil things.
In every place the eyes of the Lord watch the good and the evil.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, and those who guard it will be filled with the spirit.
A fool despises his father's instruction, but whoever heeds reproof is discerning. As righteousness increases, there is great strength, and the ungodly will perish, uprooted from the earth.
The houses of the righteous have great strength, but the fruits of the ungodly will perish.
The lips of the wise are established in wisdom, but the hearts of the foolish are not free from error.
The sacrifices of the ungodly are defiled before God, but the vows of the upright are acceptable to him.
The ways of the ungodly are defiled before the Lord, but he loves whoever follows righteousness.
The instruction of the innocent is recognized by their neighbors, but those who hate reproof will end in disgrace.
Hell and destruction are open before the Lord; how could human hearts not also be?
An undisciplined person does not love those who reprove him, and he will not converse with the wise.
When the heart rejoices, the face blossoms, but a spirit in sorrow goes about grieving.
An upright heart seeks wisdom, but the mouth of the undisciplined becomes familiar with evil.
At all times the eyes of the evil look for evil things, but the good are at peace at every hour.
A small portion with the fear of the Lord is better than great treasures without reverence.
A feast of vegetables with love and kindness is better than a stall-fed calf with hatred.
An angry man stirs up quarrels, but a patient man calms even a quarrel about to arise. A patient man puts an end to disputes, but an ungodly man provokes them still further.
The paths of the fainthearted are covered with thorns, but those of the diligent are cultivated.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son despises his mother.
The heart of a fool lacks understanding, but a wise man walks uprightly.
Those who do not honor their advisers delay their plans. A plan is established in the hearts of advisers.
And a fool does not submit to it, nor will he say anything fitting and good for everyone.
The counsel of the wise is the path of life, so that one may turn away from hell and be saved.
The Lord destroys the houses of the insolent and establishes the boundaries of orphans and widows.
An unjust plan is defiled before the Lord, but the words of the holy are pure.
Whoever takes bribes destroys his own life, but whoever hates bribes will live. Through mercy and faithfulness sins are cleansed, and through the fear of the Lord everyone turns away from evil.

The hearts of the righteous meditate on faith, but the mouth of the ungodly answers with evil things. The ways of righteous people are acceptable before the Lord; for their sake even enemies become friends.
God is far from the ungodly, but he hears the prayers of the righteous.

It is better to receive a little with righteousness than abundant profits without reverence. Let a man's heart consider what is right, so that his steps may be directed by God. An eye that sees good things makes the heart glad, and good news nourishes the bones.
Whoever rejects instruction hates himself, but whoever heeds reproof gains understanding.
The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom, and the beginning of glory will answer him.
It is for a person to lay matters in his heart, but the answer of the tongue comes from the Lord.
All the deeds of the humble person are manifest before God, and the Lord establishes spirits.
Commit your works to the Lord, and your plans will be established. The greater you become, the more you should keep yourself humble, and you will find favor before the Lord.
The Lord made everything for himself, but the ungodly will perish on an evil day.

Everyone who is arrogant is unclean before the Lord. Whoever attacks without cause will not be justified. The beginning of a good path is to practice righteousness, and prayers are more acceptable to God than offering sacrifices.
Whoever seeks the Lord will find knowledge together with righteousness, and those who seek him uprightly will find peace.
For all God's works are done in righteousness; the ungodly person is kept for an evil day.
It is better to receive a little with the fear of the Lord than great treasures with ungodliness.
Let a man's heart consider what is right, so that his steps may be directed by God.
Prophecy is on the lips of a king, and let his mouth not go astray in judgment.
The balance of the scales is justice from the Lord, and his works are just weights.
Someone who does evil is abhorrent to a king, for the throne of his authority is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are acceptable to a king; the Lord loves upright words.
A king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise man calms him.
The king's son is in the light of life, and those acceptable to him are like a cloud of late rain.
The resting places of wisdom are more desirable than gold; the resting places of understanding are more desirable than silver.

The paths of life turn away from evil; the ways of righteousness bring long life. Whoever accepts instruction will prosper, and whoever keeps correction will become wise. Whoever takes care to follow the Lord's ways preserves his own life; whoever loves life should restrain his mouth.
Acts of contempt are reckoned before destruction, and malice before a fall.
It is better to be calm-hearted and humble than to divide plunder with those who act contemptuously.
Whoever handles matters wisely finds good, and whoever trusts in the Lord is blessed.
They call the wise and intelligent fools, and those whose words are sweet will hear still more.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who possess it, but the instruction of fools is evil.
The heart of a wise man understands what comes from his own mouth, and he will ponder knowledge of what is right with his lips.
Good words are a honeycomb, and their sweetness is healing for souls.
There are paths that seem straight to a person, but their end leads to the depths of hell.
A man toils for himself and forces his own destruction, but the crooked man carries destruction in his mouth.
A foolish man digs up evil for himself and stores up fire on his lips.
A cunning man [?] evil, and the lamp of deceit is kindled by evil and separates friends.
A lawless man repeatedly puts his friends to the test and leads them along evil paths.
The man who fixes his eyes and plots perverse things, and decrees every evil with his lips, is a furnace of evil.
Old age is a crown of honor, and it is found on the paths of righteousness.
A patient man is better than a mighty man, and a man who possesses wisdom is better than vast estates; one who overcomes anger is better than one who captures a mighty city.
Everything returns again into the lap of the unjust, but justice for everyone comes from the Lord.
Better one tasty morsel with peace than houses full of slaughtered animals and good things with hostility.
A wise servant will rule over foolish masters and share a portion with the brothers.
As silver and gold are tested in furnaces, so God examines hearts.
The tongue of the lawless obeys evil, but the righteous person pays no attention to lying lips. For the faithful, the whole world is full of riches; for the faithless, there is not even a small coin.
Whoever mocks a poor person angers that person's Creator, and whoever kicks someone who is ruined will not be acquitted; but those who show compassion will find mercy.
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and children take pride in their fathers.
Faithful lips do not suit fools, nor do lying lips suit the righteous.
Instruction is a reward of grace for those who carry it, for wherever it turns, it will succeed.
Whoever conceals offenses seeks friendship, but whoever hates concealing them separates friends and family.
Threats crush the hearts of the wise, but a fool pays no attention even if he receives many blows.
Every malicious person stirs up disputes, but the Lord sends a merciless angel against him.
Anxiety will fall into the heart of a wise man, but fools plot evil.
If someone repays evil for good, may evil never depart from his house.
The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, and conflict and strife lead to poverty.
Whoever declares the unjust righteous and whoever declares the righteous unjust are both unclean and detestable before the Lord.
Why does a fool have possessions? For a fool cannot understand wisdom. Whoever builds his house high seeks its destruction, and whoever stubbornly resists instruction will fall into trouble.
Let there be friends for you at all times, but let brothers be of use to you in trouble, for that is the very reason they are born.
A foolish man dances and rejoices when he becomes guarantor for his friend.
The lover of harm rejoices in strife; whoever raises his house high seeks its destruction.
The hardhearted person meets with no good; a man with a wavering tongue will fall into trouble.
A fool’s heart is a grief to those who bore him. A father does not rejoice over an undisciplined son; a wise son makes his mother glad.
A joyful heart brings cheer; the bones of an anxious man dry up.
The ways of one who unjustly takes a bribe into his lap do not prosper; the wicked man turns aside from the paths of righteousness.
The countenance of a discerning man is wise; a fool’s eyes wander aimlessly.
A foolish son is a source of anger to his father and of pain to those who bore him.
It is not good to punish a righteous man, nor to plot against righteous rulers over matters of justice.
Whoever refrains from uttering a harsh word is wise; a patient man has understanding.
They asked the fool whether there was any wisdom and whether it would be counted as wisdom. He fell silent and was considered wise.
A man who wishes to break away from his friends seeks excuses; he will be reproached at all times.
Wisdom is of no use to a senseless man, for he behaves all the more foolishly.
When a wicked man reaches the depths of evil, he becomes contemptuous, but dishonor and reproach come upon him.
The counsel in a man’s heart is deep water, a flowing river and a fountain of life.
It is not good to show partiality to the wicked, nor to pervert the rights of the righteous in judgment.
A fool’s lips bring him into trouble, and his mouth brazenly calls down death upon him.
A fool’s mouth is his destruction, and his lips are a snare for his own life.
Fear destroys the coward; the souls of effeminate men will go hungry.
Whoever does not heal himself in his work is a brother to one who does [?] to himself.
The Lord’s name is known by the greatness of his power, and the righteous who run to him are raised up.
A rich man’s possessions are a fortified city, and his glory provides great shelter.
Before destruction a man’s heart grows proud, and before gaining esteem he humbles himself.
Whoever gives an answer before hearing anything brings folly and reproach upon himself.
A wise servant calms a man’s anger, but who can endure a short-tempered man?
A wise person’s heart acquires understanding; the ears of the wise seek counsel.
A person's gifts make room for him and seat him among rulers.
A righteous person accuses himself at the beginning of his speech, so that when his opponent begins, the opponent is put to shame.
The silent one quietly settles disputes and decides matters between powerful men.
A brother helped by a brother is like a strong, fortified city, raised up like a firmly established kingdom.
A man fills his belly with the fruit of his mouth, and he will be satisfied with the fruit of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and whoever masters it will eat its fruit.
Whoever has found a good wife has found favor and received joy from God. Whoever sends away a good wife sends away good things, and whoever keeps an adulterous wife is foolish and ungodly.
The poor man resorts only to pleading words, but the rich man gives a bold answer.
A man goes shamelessly into a brothel. A nearby friend is better than a distant brother.
An ignorant person who walks with integrity is better than a fool with loose lips.
Yet ignorance is not good for a person, and he sins when he hurries his feet.
A man's foolishness ruins his ways, and in his heart he blames God.
Wealth adds many friends, but a poor person is separated even from his own friend.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever makes an accusation without cause will not escape.
Many flatter kings, and every malicious person becomes a disgrace among people.

Everyone who hates a poor brother is also far from his love. Good counsel draws near to those who recognize it, and a wise man will find it. Whoever does great evil brings evil to completion, and whoever stirs up words will not escape, especially whoever handles words that are not his own.
Whoever acquires understanding loves himself, and whoever preserves wisdom preserves good things.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever kindles wickedness among his companions and stirs up evil will perish.
Luxury is not fitting for a fool, nor is it fitting for a servant to begin ruling arrogantly.
A merciful man is patient, and his grounds for boasting rise above those of fools.
A king's threats are like a lion's roaring; his cheerfulness is like dew upon green grass.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father. Vows made from the wages of hired workers are not holy.
Fathers divide houses and possessions among their sons, but a wife is matched to a man by the Lord.
Cowardice grips an effeminate person; a person who hates work will go hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandments preserves his life, and whoever disregards his own way will perish.
Whoever has mercy on the needy lends to God, and God will repay him according to what he has given.
Discipline your son, so that you may have good hope, and do not be arrogant in your insults. For if you strike him with a rod, he will not die; rather, you will save his life from death.
A man who acts wickedly will suffer much, and if he becomes still more vicious, he will put his own life at stake as well.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, so that you may be wise in the end.
There are many plans in a man's heart, but God's purpose remains forever.
A man's fruit is his mercy. A righteous poor man is better than a rich liar.
The fear of the Lord leads a man to life, but the fearless man, wandering at the gates, will dwell in places where there will never be any visitation.
Whoever hides his hands in his bosom does so in vain; he will not even bring them to his mouth.
When a fool is punished, the innocent become still more discerning; but if you rebuke a wise man, he will take understanding to heart.
A son who dishonors his father and rejects his mother bears shame and will be an object of reproach.
A son who ceases to observe his father's instruction devises evil words.
Whoever stands surety for a foolish youth insults justice, and the mouth of the ungodly swallows judgments.
Torments are prepared for those who reject instruction, and likewise punishments for fools.
Wine is unruly, and drunkenness is abusive, and everyone who becomes involved with them is not wise.
A king's punishment is no less than a lion's rage, and whoever provokes him harms his own life.
It is a man's glory to turn away from insults, but every fool becomes entangled in such things.
Even when a lazy man is reproached, he is not ashamed; neither is the one who borrows grain in summer.
The purpose in a man's heart is deep water, but a wise man will draw it out.
A merciful man is great and honorable, but it is hard to find a faithful man.
Whoever walks blamelessly in righteousness will leave blessed children behind him.
When a righteous king sits on the throne, no evildoer will stand against his gaze.
Who will boast of having a pure heart, or who will dare to say that he is free from sins?

A large weight and a small one, and a double measure, are both abominable before God. They will be brought to nothing, as will those who make them; even in his conduct a man will be brought to nothing.
A young man who lives in purity has upright paths.
The ear hears and the eye sees; both are the work of the Lord.
Do not love speaking evil, lest you perish. Open your eyes and be satisfied with bread.
The one who acquires it calls it bad, but after going away, he boasts of it.
There is gold and an abundance of gems, but lips of knowledge are a precious vessel.
Take away his garment, for he stood surety for a stranger and pledged it in hospitality.
The bread of deceit tasted sweet to a man, but his mouth will be filled with gravel.
Let plans be prepared thoughtfully, and let war be waged with wisdom.
One who reveals secrets acts deceitfully; do not associate with one who deceives with his lips.
Whoever curses his father or mother, his light will be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes will see darkness.
An inheritance acquired hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, “I will take revenge on my enemy.” Instead, wait for the Lord, so that he may be your helper.
A double measure is abhorrent before the Lord, and a deceitful weight is not good in his sight.
A man's steps are directed by the Lord; how can a mortal understand his own ways?
It is a snare for a man to act hastily and dedicate something from his possessions, for after making the vow comes regret.
A wise king scatters the ungodly and drives a wheel over them.
The human spirit is the Lord's light, which searches the storehouses of the heart.
Mercy and truth are a king's guardians, and they will surround his throne with righteousness.
Wisdom is the adornment of young men, and gray hair is the glory of the old.
Wounds and blows befall the wicked, and torments reach the chambers of the belly.
Like streams of water, a king's heart is in God's hands; he turns it in whatever direction he wishes it to face.
Every man seems righteous to himself, but the Lord directs hearts.
Doing righteousness and speaking truth are more pleasing before the Lord than the blood of sacrifices.
A hardhearted man is arrogant in his insults; the [?] of the ungodly is sin.
A concise plan leads only to abundance, but everyone who acts hastily leads only to scarcity.
Whoever gathers treasures with a lying tongue pursues vain things and falls into the snares of death.
Destruction will overtake the ungodly, because they are unwilling to do what is just.
God sends a crooked path to the crooked, for his works are pure and upright.
It is better to live in a corner under the open sky than in plastered rooms with injustice and in a house of turmoil.
The soul of the ungodly desires evil, and he will find mercy from no one.
When the foolish person is punished, the innocent becomes still more discerning; through wisdom, the perceptive person receives knowledge.
The righteous person considers the heart of the ungodly, and evils destroy the ungodly.
Whoever stops his ears so as not to hear the weak will himself cry out to the Lord, and the Lord will not hear him.
Secret gifts turn away anger, but whoever holds back gifts arouses fierce anger.
It is a joy for the righteous to do justice, but what is holy seems unclean to evildoers.
A man who strays from the path of righteousness will rest in the assembly of the giants.
A poor man loves pleasure; whoever loves wine and oil [?] wealth.
The lawless person becomes a ransom for the righteous, and those who break the covenant for the upright.
It is better to live in the wilderness than with a foolish, talkative, and angry wife.
Desirable treasure will rest in the mouth of the wise, but foolish men will swallow it.
The path of righteousness and mercy will find life, righteousness, and glory.
Wisdom came against fortified cities and demolished the strongholds in which the ungodly had trusted.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue keeps himself from trouble.
The harsh, brazen, and proud are called vile, and whoever bears grudges is lawless.
Desires kill the lazy man, because his hands are unwilling to do any work.
Every day the ungodly person longs for evil things, but the righteous person shows mercy and gives without holding back.
The sacrifices of the ungodly are unclean before the Lord, for they offer them with lawlessness.
A false witness will perish, but an obedient man will speak cautiously.
An ungodly man acts with brazen defiance, but the upright man understands his own ways.
There is no human wisdom, courage, or counsel against God.
A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but help comes from the Lord.
A good name is better than great wealth, and good favor is better than silver and gold.
The rich and the poor meet one another; the Lord watches over them both.
A discerning person, seeing the evildoer punished, firmly disciplines himself; the foolish passed by them and suffered harm.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and wealth, glory, and life.
Thorns and snares lie in the paths of the crooked, but whoever guards his own life will keep away from them.
The training of a young man is in accordance with his ways; even when he grows old, he will not depart from them.
The poor will rule over the rich, and servants will lend to their masters.
Whoever sows folly will reap evil and suffer the full punishment for his deeds.

God loves a cheerful and generous man. Whoever shows mercy to the poor will himself be fed, because he gave the poor some of his own bread. Whoever gives a bribe gains victory and honor, but kills the souls of those who receive it.
Drive the wicked man out of the assembly, and strife will leave with him, for whenever he sits in the assembly, he insults everyone.
The Lord loves a pure heart, and all who are blameless are acceptable to him. A king shepherds with his lips.
The eyes of the Lord preserve understanding, and he despises lawless words.
The coward makes excuses and says, “A lion occupies the roads, and there are murderers in the passages through the squares.”

The mouth of a lawless person is a deep pit, and whoever is hated by the Lord will fall into it. Evil paths lie before a man, and he does not like to turn away from them, but one must turn away from a crooked and evil path.
Foolishness burns in a young man's heart; the rod and discipline are far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor brings much evil upon himself, and whoever gives to the rich is left in need.
Turn your ear toward the words of the wise, listen to my words, and strengthen your heart so that you may know that they are good.
And if you place them in your heart, they will rejoice together on your lips.
So that your hope may be in the Lord, and he may show you his ways.
And write them within yourself three times, for counsel, knowledge, and understanding.
Look, I teach you true words and knowledge, so that you may obediently answer with words of truth those who approach you.
Do not oppress the needy because he is poor, and do not dishonor the needy at the gates.
For the Lord will plead his case and rescue your soul from being plundered.
Do not become the companion of an angry man, and do not live with a wrathful friend.
Otherwise you may learn his ways and bring a noose upon your own soul.
Do not offer yourself as a guarantor out of partiality.
For if you have nothing with which to repay, they will take the bedding from beneath your body.
Do not move the ancient boundary markers that your fathers set up.
A man who is quick and careful in his work should be placed before kings, not before fainthearted men.
When you sit down for dinner to eat at the table of the powerful, carefully consider what is set before you, and then reach out your hand.
Know that you too must prepare something like this.
But if you are very greedy, do not desire his delicacies, for this very thing goes hand in hand with the falsehood of life.
Do not strive to impoverish yourself alongside a rich man; rather, in your wisdom, withdraw from him.
If you fix your eyes on him, he will be nowhere to be seen, for he is preparing wings for himself like an eagle's and returns to his patriarch's house.
Do not eat bread with an evil-eyed man, and do not desire his food.
He eats and drinks as though someone were swallowing a hair.
Do not bring him into your home, and do not eat your bread with him, for he will make it repulsive and corrupt your good words.
Do not speak at all in the hearing of a fool, lest he despise your wise words.
Do not move the ancient boundaries, and do not enter the possessions of orphans.
For the Lord who redeems them is mighty, and he will plead their case against you.
Apply your heart to instruction, and prepare your ears for words of wisdom.
Do not hold back from disciplining a child, for if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
You strike him with a rod, but you save his life from death.
My son, if your heart becomes wise, you will make my heart rejoice too.
And if you join your lips to my lips, provided that you are upright.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always be diligent in fearing the Lord.
For if you keep it, you will have offspring, and your hope will not be rejected.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and set the thoughts of your heart straight.
Do not be a drunkard, and do not envy those who pool their resources to buy meat.
For every drunkard and frequenter of prostitutes will become poor, and everyone who sleeps will be clothed in rags.
Listen, my son, to the father who begot you, and do not despise your mother's old age.
Acquire truth, and do not abandon wisdom, instruction, or understanding.
A righteous father provides a good upbringing, and his heart rejoices over a wise son.
Let your father and mother rejoice in you, and let the woman who bore you be glad.
Give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes attend to my ways.
A stranger's house is a jar full of holes, and a foreign woman is a narrow well.
For such a person will quickly perish, and every lawless person will be destroyed.
Who has woe? Who has turmoil? Who has lawsuits? Who has troubles and anxieties? Who has wounds without cause? Who has bruised eyes?
Is it not those who linger over wine and look for places where drinking parties are held?

Do not get drunk on wine, but converse with righteous people, and speak with one another in the public squares. But if you let your eyes wander over bowls and cups, afterward you will go about more naked than a pestle.
And in the end you will stretch out like someone bitten by a snake, and venom will spread as from a viper.
When your eyes see a foreign woman, your mouth will then speak perverse things.
And you will fall and lie in the heart of the sea, like a helmsman amid a violent storm.
And you will say, “They struck me, but I felt no pain; they mocked me, but I did not know it. When will morning come, so that I may get up and seek someone to keep company with?”
My son, do not envy the wicked, and do not desire to be with them.
For their hearts devise falsehood, and their lips speak of harm.
A house is built by wisdom and established by understanding.
And by counsel its storerooms are filled with every kind of precious and good wealth.
A wise person is better than a strong one, and a person of understanding is better than someone who owns great estates.
War is waged with guidance and with the help of a discerning heart.
Wisdom and good counsel are at the gates of the wise.
The wise do not turn aside from the Lord’s words, but deliberate in their assemblies.
Death overtakes those without instruction, and the foolish die in their sins.
Abomination makes the evildoer filthy on the day of evil and on the day of distress, until he is destroyed.
Rescue those who are being led to death, and redeem those condemned to die; do not hold back.
But if you say, “I do not know him, nor does he know me,” know that the Lord knows everyone's heart. He who created everyone's breath knows everything and repays each person according to their deeds.
Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and honeycomb, so that your throat may taste its sweetness.
Let the understanding of wisdom be the same within you, for if you find it, your end will be good, and your light will not fail.
Do not bring the ungodly into the pastures of the righteous, and do not be deceived by a full belly.
For even if the righteous person falls seven times, he will rise, but the ungodly will grow weak amid troubles.
If your enemy falls, do not stamp your feet, and when he stumbles, do not become arrogant.
Otherwise the Lord may see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
Do not rejoice over evildoers, and do not envy sinners.
For the wicked will have no offspring, and the lamp of the ungodly will be extinguished.
Fear God, my son, and the king, and do not rebel against either of them.
For they will suddenly call the ungodly to account, and who knows the punishment that comes from them both?
I say this to you who are wise: do not be ashamed to understand justice. Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
Whoever says of the ungodly, “He is righteous,” will be cursed by the peoples and hated by the nations.
But those who rebuke them will be seen as good, and a blessing of good things will come upon them.
Lips will love replies of good words, and whoever answers with opposing words prepares for himself words of departure.
Prepare your work outside, and make preparations on your estates; follow me, and you will rebuild your house.
Do not be a false witness against your neighbor, and do not speak loosely with your lips.
Do not say, “As he treated me, so I will treat him; I will repay him as he defrauded me.”
A foolish man is like a field, and a man lacking sense is like a vineyard.
If you leave it alone, it becomes uncultivated and completely overgrown with weeds; it is abandoned, and the stones of its walls fall to the ground.
Afterward he will say, “I repented; I looked and chose instruction.”
How long will you lie there, you lazy man? When will you wake from sleep? You will sleep a little, doze a little, rest a little, and fold your hands over your chest a little.
If you do this, your poverty will come like a scout, and your need like a swift-footed messenger.
A son who heeds words will be safe from destruction, for he has indeed accepted them.
Let no lie be spoken by a king's tongue, and let no deceit come from his tongue.
A king's tongue is a sharp sword, not flesh, and whoever is handed over to him is crushed.
For if his anger is sharpened, he will destroy people, joints and all, and devour men's bones. He will burn like a flame, and become like a carcass in eagles' nests.
Fear my words, my child, and when you receive them, you will repent.
The unsearchable proverbs of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judah, wrote down.
God's glory conceals a matter; a king's glory honors commands.
Heaven is high, the earth is deep, and a king's heart is beyond examination.
Test unrefined silver, and through purification it will all become pure.
Remove the ungodly from the king's presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Do not be proud before a king, and do not approach the places of the great.
For it is better for you that someone should say, “Come up here to me,” than that you should be brought low before a powerful man.
Speak of what your eyes have seen. Do not rush boldly into a fight, lest you regret it afterward.
When your friend reproaches you, withdraw; do not disregard it, lest your friend reproach you.

And your enmity and strife will not depart, but will become like death to you. Favor and friendship are liberating; establish them within yourself so that you will not be disgraced, and spend your time in peace.
A golden apple set with carnelian—such is the speaking of wise words.
A wise word in attentive ears is a precious carnelian set in a gold earring.
As someone who brings snow helps a person overheated in summer, so a faithful messenger helps those who sent him; he benefits the souls of those who put their trust in him.
Like winds, clouds, and violent rains are those who boast of false gifts.
A king's success comes through patience; an unrestrained tongue crushes bones.
When you find honey, my child, eat it in moderation, lest you become full and vomit it up.
Do not go too often to your friend, lest he grow tired of you and hate you.
Like a sword and a sharpened arrow is a man who gives false testimony against his friend.
The ways of the wicked and the feet of the lawless will perish on an evil day.
Taking off a cloak on a cold day is as useless as vinegar on a wound. Likewise, pains that afflict the body sadden the heart. Like a moth in clothing and a worm in wood, sorrow harms a man's heart.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him something to drink.
By doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the Lord will repay you with good.
The north wind raises clouds, and shameless faces provoke the tongue.
It is better to live in a corner of the roof than in the same house with a slanderous wife.
As cold water is welcome to a thirsty person, so is good news from a distant land.
As when someone muddies a spring and pollutes its flowing waters, so it is shameful for a righteous person to fall before the ungodly.
Eating much honey is not good, but precious words ought to be honored.
Like a city whose walls have been destroyed is a man who does anything without deliberation.
Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool.
As birds and sparrows fly away, so groundless curses do not come upon anyone.
As a whip is for a horse and a goad for a donkey, so a rod is for foolish people.
Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, lest you become like him.
But answer him according to his foolishness, lest he seem very wise in his own eyes.
Whoever sends a message through a foolish messenger brings reproach upon his own ways.
Cut short the steps of the feet and the proverbs from a fool's mouth.
Whoever puts a stone in a sling is like a man who bestows honor on a fool.
A drunkard's hands become full of thorns, and service is in the hands of a fool.
All the bodies of fools are tossed about by many waves, for their follies are shattered.

As a dog becomes loathsome when it returns to its own vomit, so does a fool with his evil deeds when he returns again to his sins. There is shame that brings sins, and there is shame that brings glory and favor.
I saw a man who prided himself on being wise, but there was more hope for a fool than for him.
When you send a coward on a journey, he says, “A lion occupies the roads, and there are killers in the public squares.”
As a door turns on its hinge, so a lazy person turns on his bed.
A lazy person hides his hand in his bosom and is slow to bring it to his mouth.
A lazy person considers himself wiser than someone who brings news of greatness.
Like someone who grabs a dog by the tail is a person who gets involved in another person's dispute.
Like tempters who hurl words at people, whoever rushes to oppose the words is the first to be brought down.
So are all those who lie in wait for their friends and, when confronted, say, “We were only playing.”
A fire blazes with plentiful wood, and where there is no double-minded person, strife ceases.
A brazier is for sparks, wood is for fire, and a slanderer is for stirring up strife.
The words of deceivers are soft, but they cast people into storehouses of conflict.
Someone who gives silver deceitfully is regarded as a potsherd; smooth lips conceal sorrowful hearts.
Whoever weeps for an enemy makes everything known with his lips, but devises deceit in his heart.
If your enemy implores you and pleads loudly, do not trust him, for there are seven evils in his heart.
Whoever [?] hostility makes deceit evident; a skilled speaker conceals his wrongdoing in court.
Whoever digs a pit for his neighbor will fill it himself, and whoever rolls a stone will roll it upon himself.
A lying tongue hates truth, and an unrestrained mouth causes disturbances.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what tomorrow will bring you.
Let your neighbor praise you, not your own mouth; a stranger, not your own lips.
Stone is heavy, and sand is difficult to lift, but a fool's anger is heavier than both.
Resentment is merciless, and anger is fierce, but jealousy tolerates nothing.
An open rebuke is better than hidden friendship.
A friend's blows are better than an enemy's willful kisses.
A person who is full despises honeycomb and honey, but to a hungry person even something bitter seems sweet.
Like a bird that flies from its nest, so a person becomes enslaved when he leaves his own place for a foreign one.
Oil, incense, and wine gladden the heart, but sorrow breaks the soul.
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not enter your brother's house when you are in distress. A nearby friend is better than a brother who lives far away.
Be wise, my son, so that your heart may be glad, and turn words of reproach away from yourself.
The prudent person hid when evils came, but fools go out to meet them and will fall into punishment.
Strip his clothes from him, for the slanderer has passed by, because he was ruining another person's possessions.
Someone who praises a friend loudly in the morning should be considered no better than someone who curses him.
A dripping leak drives a man from his house on a winter day; likewise, a foolish wife drives her husband from his house.
The north wind is fierce, but it is called “right.”
Iron sharpens iron, and a man provokes his companion.
Whoever plants a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever looks after his master will be honored.
Just as faces are not alike, neither are people's hearts alike.
Hell and destruction are insatiable, and so are the eyes of greedy people. Whoever lets his eyes wander is detestable before the Lord, as are those who are undisciplined and unrestrained in speech.
Silver and gold are tested in furnaces, and a man is tested by the mouths of those who praise him.

The heart of a lawless person seeks evil, and an upright heart seeks knowledge. Even if you strike a fool in the middle of an assembly and disgrace him, you still will not drive his foolishness out of him.
Be diligent in knowing your sheep, and set your heart on your herds.
For a man's strength, might, and authority do not last forever, nor have they been given to him from generation to generation.
Care for the plants in the field, mow the grass, and gather the green grass.
So that you may have sheep to provide clothing, tend the fields so that you may have lambs.
My child, learn from me sayings that have power to sustain the life of your household and the lives of your friends.
The wicked flee when no one is pursuing them, but the righteous are confident like a lion.
Because of the sins of the wicked, disputes arise, but a discerning man puts an end to them.
A powerful man, in his wickedness, falsely accuses the poor.
Those who abandon the law and praise wickedness are like a violent and useless rain, but those who love the law surround themselves with a wall.
Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the Lord will understand everything.
A poor person who walks in truth is better than a rich liar.
A wise son keeps the law, but whoever indulges in gluttony dishonors his father.
Whoever fills his house through interest and usury gathers it for someone who has mercy on the poor.
Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law also defiles his own vows.

Whoever leads the upright astray along an evil path will himself fall into destruction. The blameless will share in good things, and the lawless will pass by the good things; let them not enter into them.
A rich man seems wise to himself, but a discerning poor person rebukes him.
Through the help of the righteous, glory abounds, but in the places of the ungodly people perish.
Whoever conceals his wickedness will not prosper, but whoever brings it to light and condemns it will be loved.
Blessed is the man who disregards everything out of reverence, but the hardhearted will fall into troubles.
A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf is the poor man who rules over an impoverished nation.
A king lacking understanding is a great oppressor, but whoever hates injustice will live long.
