A man who stands surety for someone condemned to death becomes a fugitive and will not be secure. Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and adorn your soul, and he will not obey a lawless nation.
Whoever walks in righteousness will find help, but whoever takes a crooked path will become entangled in it.
Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever pursues empty things will have plenty of poverty.
A faithful man will be greatly blessed, and let the evildoer not escape punishment. Whoever does not respect the righteous is not worthy of praise.
It is not good to show favoritism to the lawless when reproving them; such a person sells a man for a morsel of bread.
An envious man hastens to become rich and does not know that the merciful man will overcome him.
Whoever reproves a man for his ways will receive more thanks than someone who flatters with his tongue.
Whoever rejects his father or mother and thinks he is not sinning is a companion of ungodly men.
A greedy man stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts in the Lord will live under his care.
Whoever trusts in the boldness of his own heart is foolish, but whoever walks in wisdom will be saved.
Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but whoever turns his eyes away from them will suffer great need.
In the places of the ungodly, the righteous groan, but when the ungodly perish, the righteous multiply.
A man who reproves is better than a stubborn man, for when fire suddenly strikes him, there will be no cure.
When the righteous are praised, the peoples will rejoice; under the rule of the ungodly, the righteous groan.
The father of a man who loves wisdom will rejoice, but whoever supports prostitutes squanders his wealth.
A righteous king establishes the land, but a lawless man destroys it.
Whoever stirs up quarrels in front of his friend will entangle his own feet in snares.
A powerful snare will be set for a sinful man, but the righteous will have joy and gladness.
The righteous knows how to judge the poor, but the ungodly does not understand knowledge, and the poor man has no thoughts of justice.
Lawless men set a city on fire, but the wise turn away anger.
A wise man judges nations, but a foolish man is mocked when he becomes angry, and he feels no fear.
Bloodthirsty men hate the righteous, but the upright will cherish his life.
A fool pours out all his anger at once, but the wise man bears it calmly.
A king who listens to unjust words has only lawless people around him.
When lender and borrower meet together, the Lord takes account of both.
A king who judges the poor truthfully will have his throne established as a testimony.
Beatings and rebukes give wisdom, but a wayward child brings shame on his parents.
When the ungodly multiply, sins increase, but the righteous are struck with fear at their downfall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and bring honor to your soul.
No leader will be found for a lawless nation, but whoever keeps the law is blessed.
A stubborn servant is not disciplined by words; even if he understands, he does not heed them.
When you see a man rash in his words, know that there is more hope for a fool than for him.
One who is pampered from childhood will be handed over into slavery and afterward will be tormented in his soul.
An angry man stirs up strife, a gentle man puts an end to sins, and a wrathful man digs up sins.
Arrogance brings a man low, but the Lord gives glory to the humble.
Whoever shares with thieves hates himself; those who hear an oath put before them and do not report it

will be exposed through fear and shame before people and will be ruined. But whoever trusts in the Lord will be joyful. A man's ungodliness brings a stumbling block, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be saved.
Many flatter rulers, but a man's justice comes from the Lord.
A lawless man is an abomination to the righteous, and an upright path is an abomination to the lawless.
This is what the man says to those who believe in God: If I remain silent,
it is because I am more foolish than all people, and human wisdom is not in me.
God taught me wisdom, and I gained understanding of the knowledge of the holy ones, and I know holy things.

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the winds into his lap? Who has wrapped the waters in his garments? Who has taken hold of the ends of the earth? What is his name, or what is his son's name, so that you may know that
all the words of God are tested, and he watches over those who fear him.
Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you prove to be a liar.
I ask two things of you; do not withhold your favors from me before I die:
Keep empty words and lies far from me. Give me neither wealth nor poverty, but weigh out for me a sufficient portion of what I need,
lest I become rich and lie and say, “Who will see me?” Or lest I become poor and steal and swear by the name of my God.
Do not hand a servant over to his master, lest he curse you and you be ruined.
An evil offspring curses his father and does not bless his mother.
An evil generation counts itself among the righteous but has not washed away its own filth.
An evil generation has arrogant eyes and is proud in its eyelids.
An evil generation has teeth like swords and fangs like knives, to consume and devour the lowly of the earth and the poor among humankind.
The leech had three dearly loved daughters, and these three did not satisfy it, and the fourth was not filled enough to say, “Enough.”
Hell and destruction, the love of women and Tartarus, and the earth that is not satisfied with water; and water and fire never say, “Enough.”
The eye that scorns a father and dishonors a mother’s old age—the ravens of the valleys will pluck it out, and the young eagles will tear it to pieces.
There are three things that I cannot understand, and a fourth that I do not know:
the tracks of an eagle in flight, the paths of a snake on a rock, the trails of a ship traveling through the sea, and the paths of a young man.
Such also is the way of an adulterous woman: when she has done something, she washes and says, “I have done nothing.”
Under three things the earth shakes, and under a fourth it cannot remain still:
if a slave becomes king, and if a fool has his fill of bread;
and if a maidservant drives out her mistress, and if a hated woman finds a good husband.
There are four things that are small on the earth, yet they are wiser than the wise:
the ant, which has no strength, yet prepares its food in summer;
and rabbits, a powerless kind, which make their homes among the rocks;
the locust has no king, yet gathers in an orderly army as though at a single command;
and the spider, which clings to a wall with its hands and is easy to catch, dwells in the palaces of kings.
There are three that walk proudly, and a fourth that strides beautifully.
A lion cub is stronger than the other animals; it does not fear them or turn its back on them.
And a rooster struts among the hens, and a male goat leads the flock, and a king speaks publicly among the nations.
If you give yourself over to ease and stretch your hand toward your mouth in a quarrel, you will be dishonored.
Draw out milk, and there will be butter; but if you squeeze the teats too hard, blood comes out, and if you draw out words, lawsuits and quarrels will come out.
My words are spoken by God: the instruction of a king whose mother taught him.
For, my child, these are God’s words. I speak to you, firstborn son, for you are my child, the fruit of my womb, for you are the child of my vows.
Do not give your greatness and your thoughts to women, or your life to belated regrets. Do everything with deliberation; drink wine with deliberation.
Let hot-tempered rulers not drink wine,
lest, when they drink, they forget wisdom and become unable to judge the weak fairly.
Give intoxicating drink to those who are sorrowful, and wine to drink to those in pain,
so that they may drink and forget their poverty and remember their suffering no more.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge everyone with sound judgment.
And distinguish and judge the destitute and the weak.
If an industrious woman is found, such a woman is more valuable than precious stones.
Her husband's heart trusts in her; such a man will never lack gain.
She is her husband's partner in all the good things of life, and not in evil things.
Having found wool and linen, she made useful articles with her own hands.
She became like a profitable ship, gathering her treasures from far away.
She rises at dawn and gives food to her household and work to her maidservants.
She sees a beautiful field and buys it, and with the fruit of her hands she cultivates the land.
She girded her waist with strength and put her arms to work.
She tasted how pleasant it is to work, and her lamp does not go out all night.
She stretches out her hands to useful work and tirelessly applies her fingers to the spindle.
She opened her hands to the poor and held out produce to the needy.
Her husband has no concern about the household when he stays somewhere away from home, for everyone with her is clothed in double garments.
She made fine linen and purple garments for her husband, and coverings for herself.
Her husband is distinguished at the gates when he sits in the assembly among the elders and inhabitants of the land.
She made linen cloth and sold it, and coverings for the Canaanites.
She clothed herself in strength and splendor, and rejoiced in the days to come.
She opened her mouth with moderation and wisdom, and kept her tongue in order.
The ways of her household are orderly, and she has not eaten the bread of idleness.
Her acts of mercy raised up her sons and made them great, and her husband praises her and says:
“Many daughters have attained greatness, and many have acted mightily, but you have excelled and surpassed them all.”
Deceptive charms and a woman's empty beauty are not in you, for a wise and devout woman will be blessed; she will honor those who fear the Lord.
Give her some of the fruit of her lips, and let her husband be praised at the gates. For a man's ways will go before his face and prosper forever and ever.
